I'd like to ask a pretty interesting question here: did you warm up to Snape after reading "The Prince's Tale" in Deathly Hallows? Snape has been one of the most controversial characters in the entire series, and after dealing with Snape's role in Deathly Hallows up until this point, you might have been ready to duel him yourself.

Did the chapter clarify him for you? Did your approval of him or his actions increase? Did you feel pity or empathy for him? I'm curious to know.
Did your opinion of Severus Snape change after "The Prince's Tale"?

Snape's always been one of my favorite characters, even before I knew his true motives. His look, demeanor, and no nonsense attitude were great traits for me. After reading "The Prince's Tale", it fully solidified him as my favorite character in the entire series. Being one of the most dynamic and caring characters, Snape really moved me in his dedication to good and Lily.

By the end of Half Blood Prince, I was already convinced that a) Snape wasn't actually evil, and b) Harry was a Horcrux. Guess (a) is relevant here in that as a result, my opinion of Snape didn't really change after Deathly Hallows. Also, I read a fair amount of fanfiction back in the day, and there was very little in "The Prince's Tale" that wasn't already postulated at some point or another. ^^

Anyways, as far as characters go, I think Snape is very well characterized and multidimensional, but no, the chapter didn't make me like him more, especially because it was implied that the only reason he remained good was because of his unrequited love for Lily. What definitely made me like him more, however, was all his actions prior to the chapter. He basically died as an unsung martyr (as far as he was concerned) in the end, which makes him pretty brave.

I agree completely with your analysis of Snape's character.

Question, though. How'd you go about realising Harry was a horcrux? That was a pretty interesting twist to me.

:) Several things gave it away for me! First, Dumbledore speculated at some point in Half Blood Prince that Nagini was a horcrux, which opened up the possibility that a living being could be a horcrux. Then I remembered that Harry had a vision as Nagini (attacking Mr. Weasley) his fifth year, meaning that Harry was connected to Nagini as he was to Voldemort, somehow. Horcruxes seemed like a super plausible common connection.

What cinched it for me though, was remembering that Dumbledore had a "gleam of triumph" in his eyes after the 4th book, when Harry's blood was taken to resurrect Voldemort. I didn't come to the correct conclusion as a result, but I did infer that Dumbledore knew something sneaky, and that something was probably that Harry was a horcrux!

Also I figured it'd make for an interesting plot, haha. :)

To play devil's advocate, I think people find Snape fascinating because he gets up to interesting things and subverts expectations.

Take his actions in book 1, for example. Yes, he was a complete ass to Harry, and it's super obvious that the guy has serious issues. And yet, he tries to save everyone from evil Quirrell, while looking completely evil himself. The reveal at the end of Book 1 was amazing as a result, and Snape was a huge part of that.

I also think a lot of people empathized with Snape after the pensieve scene in Book 5. The way he was treated by the Marauders was horrific, and while it certainly doesn't justify his behavior towards Harry, it provides a lot of realistic and believable motivation for his actions.

I would argue that most book readers have allowed themselves to fall into some form of Stockholm syndrome for Snape. Aw, he was bullied in school, poor guy. Aw, he fell in love but was rejected, how sad. That explains why he's such an asshole! And he helps sometimes, so he's just tragically admirable.

Here's the beef: instead of growing as a person and leaving his past behind him (which would have given him a much stronger character arc BTW), he remains rotten and mean. Pathetic! Can you imagine going to your school reunion and seeing that the weird creep is still a weird creep? AND now he teaches at a boarding school! First, you'd think he had a mental disorder, and second, you'd be concerned for the kids he teaches.

The worst of it is, every time someone tries to justify or stand up for Snape, it always comes back to his life as a teenager. Well let me tell you, worse things have happened to better people. Snape was just too weak to improve himself. What kind of wizard therapists are available? Because I'm certain that he never met one. At best, Snape can be described as "not completely terrible." What a swell guy.

Snape also does some undeniably good things, such as trying to out Quirrell, helping with the Horcrux hunt, and dealing for Voldemort's shit for years as a spy. Again, that doesn't mean he's a saint. He's super flawed, and he's an ass, but he has dimensions beyond being just an ass, which again makes him interesting from a literary perspective. I'm not saying he's a "swell guy." I'm saying he's an interesting guy (esp. in comparison to, say, Draco Malfoy)

But to each their own.
